input:
The project is currently facing a staffing gap that now stands at 7 weeks, and it is important to understand both how this gap has arisen and what is being done in response. The gap has been opened by departures from the engineering team, and the remaining workload has continued to be carried by the same team without any corresponding reduction in scope, which has placed sustained pressure on the staff who remain. The gap falls on the design work that feeds the EPC contractor, and each additional week that it persists effectively moves the affected packages by the same amount, creating a knock-on effect that is difficult to recover later in the programme.

Recovery through overtime working has broadly reached its limit, given that the team is already working extended hours and that the board has been clear that the quality of the issued drawings should not be traded for speed. The mitigation that is therefore proposed is the engagement of a contract engineer through the existing framework, assigned to the project manager, who owns the recovery plan and reports progress to the project board. The contract engineer would take on the checking and revision work that currently queues behind the design engineers, thereby releasing the design engineers for the packages on the critical path. The arrangement would run until the gap closes and would be reviewed at each board meeting against the recovery plan.

Recruitment for the vacant posts is continuing in parallel under its own process, although its outcome does not change the mitigation set out above, which has been sized on the gap as it currently stands. Should the departures continue, the gap would widen beyond the figure stated here, and the mitigation would then need to be revisited by the project board.
